title: Enterprise Onboarding, QBR, and Escalation Playbook
author: Samira Al-Khalili
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook combines the standard enterprise onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation paths, known issues & workarounds, support process, and QBR/health-check cadence for Redwood Inference enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE responders.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments, and high-volume Hosted API customers with an enterprise support plan).
- Covers onboarding milestones from kickoff through first production rollout, recurring health checks and QBRs, and a three-tier escalation ladder for critical incidents and regressions.

Owner & Contacts
----------------
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (CS) \u2014 Samira Al-Khalili
- Primary on-call: Customer Success Escalations Slack channel (#cs-escalations)
- SE integration lead: assigned per-customer (see account SDR/AE record)
- SRE escalation: paging via PagerDuty service: RDW-Core-SRE

Onboarding Checklist (90-day recommended cadence)
------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-kickoff (Owner: SE)
   - Share onboarding packet: architecture options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), network requirements, and data handling requirements.
   - Verify contract terms: capacity, SLAs, and compliance requirements (e.g., SOC2, HIPAA).

2) Week 0 \u2014 Kickoff (Owner: CS + SE)
   - Attendees: Customer engineering leads, network/security, product owner, CS, SE, and SRE on-call.
   - Agenda: goals, success criteria, timeline, communication plan, escalation contacts, and access matrix.
   - Deliverable: Project Plan (Jira board + shared Confluence space).

3) Week 1\u20132 \u2014 Environment & Access (Owner: SE)
   - Provisioning: Dedicated pool or Private control plane access.
   - Validate: network egress/ingress, firewall rules, KMS/HSM integration (if applicable), and DNS entries.
   - Credentials: API keys, role-based access (RBAC) mapping.
   - Checklist table:

   | Item | Required by | Verification | Owner |
   |------|-------------|--------------|-------|
   | API key issued | Day 3 | Test token call returns 200 | SE |
   | VPC peering / VPN | Day 5 | Successful curl to health endpoint | SE / Infra |
   | KMS integration | Day 7 (if required) | Key decrypt test passes | SE / Security |

4) Week 2\u20136 \u2014 Integration & Testing (Owner: SE + Customer Eng)
   - Integration patterns: direct SDK calls, gateway proxying, batching best-practices. Provide sample configs and SDK snippets.
   - Performance baseline: run perf harness for representative workload and record P50/P95 latency and tokens/sec.
   - QA: generate a set of smoke prompts and expected ranges, add to the customers' regression test set.

5) Week 6\u201312 \u2014 Pilot & Rollout (Owner: CS + Product)
   - Canary rollout: 1\u20135% traffic, monitor cost and quality metrics.
   - Rollout checklist: latency targets met, error rates <0.5%, no QoE regressions on defined prompts.
   - Go/no-go defined in Project Plan; formal sign-off captured in Confluence.

Integration Guide \u2014 Engineering Notes
-------------------------------------
- Recommended SDK config (example):
  - retry_policy: exponential_backoff(start=200ms, max=5s)
  - batching: auto_batch=true, max_batch_tokens=2048, max_batch_size=64
  - streaming: enabled for low-latency front-ends

- Network / TLS: TLS 1.2+ enforced, mutual TLS for Private deployments if requested.
- Auth: API keys with RBAC; for Private, support OAuth2/OIDC integration (customer-managed IdP).
- Telemetry: instrument calls with x-request-id and include model_version and route in traces.

Support Process & SLAs
----------------------
- Triage hours: 24/7 for P0/P1, business hours for P2/P3 (unless an enterprise plan includes extended coverage).
- Typical response targets:
  - P0 (production down): 15 minutes to acknowledge, hourly updates until mitigation.
  - P1 (severe degradation): 1 hour to acknowledge, update every 4 hours.
  - P2 (partial impact): 4 business hours to respond.
  - P3 (general question): 2 business days.
- Channels: Support Portal (ticketing), priority email, Slack (#cs-escalations), PagerDuty for P0/P1.

Escalation Playbook (Short-form)
--------------------------------
Purpose: Rapidly route incidents to the correct engineering owner while preserving customer communications.

Escalation levels:
1) Level 1 \u2014 Customer Success / Support Engineer (initial triage)
   - Actions: reproduce, collect logs (request_id, timestamps, trace links), confirm scope and impact, apply known workaround if available.
   - Escalate to Level 2 if: cannot reproduce in 30 minutes, or issue affects >10% of customer traffic.

2) Level 2 \u2014 Solutions Engineering / Product Engineering
   - Actions: deeper debugging, review model variants, check rate limits, inspect routing policies, validate KV cache behavior and batching heuristics.
   - Escalate to Level 3 if: root cause unclear after 2 hours or if remediation requires infra actions.

3) Level 3 \u2014 SRE / Runtime Engineering (PagerDuty)
   - Actions: hotfixes, capacity adjustments, kernel/runtime rollbacks, coordination with infra for GPU capacity.
   - Communication: Provide status updates per SLA, run RCA and publish postmortem for P0 incidents.

Escalation checklist (ticket fields):
- Customer name, environment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), severity, first_seen, last_updated, reproduction steps, request_ids, trace links, owner at each level.

Known Issues & Workarounds (Selection)
-------------------------------------
- High tail latency under bursty traffic (observed on older kernels): workaround \u2014 enable smaller max_batch_size (32) and reduce max_batch_tokens to 1024; enable prefix KV caching where applicable.
- Tokenization mismatch after model upgrade: workaround \u2014 pin previous model version for affected route; add regression prompts and open model-onboarding ticket.
- KMS transient errors during key rotation: workaround \u2014 fallback to cached encryption key for up to 5 minutes, alert Security and schedule emergency rotation window.

Support Playbook Examples (CLI / Snippets)
-----------------------------------------
- Health endpoint check (curl):
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
  Expected: 200 {\"status\":\"ok\",\"uptime\":\"xxh\"}

- Collect traces: include X-Request-Id header in customer reproduction; ask SRE to fetch traces via internal tracing UI: /services/rdw-core/traces?request_id=<id>

Health Checks & Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs)
--------------------------------------------------
- Health check cadence:
  - Week 4: Initial health check (onboarding-specific) \u2014 focus on integration fidelity, performance baselining, cost estimates.
  - Monthly (first 3 months post-rollout): operational health checks \u2014 latency, error-rate trends, cost per 1k tokens, model-quality regressions.
  - Quarterly: full QBR \u2014 product usage, ROI, roadmap alignment, upcoming migrations/rollouts.

- QBR template (deliverables):
  1) Executive summary (1 page): adoption, uptime, major actions.
  2) Operational metrics: P50/P95 latency, error rate, tokens/month, cost per 1k tokens.
  3) Quality metrics: regression test pass rate, recent evals, user-reported issues.
  4) Roadmap and action items: upcoming model upgrades, planned capacity increases, security/compliance milestones.

- Health thresholds to monitor (examples):
  - Availability: target 99.95% (Dedicated SLA)
  - Error budget burn: escalate when >20% of error budget consumed in a 7-day window
  - Latency: P95 < 500ms for small generations (<=256 tokens) for interactive routes
  - Cost drift: monthly cost variance >15% vs. baseline triggers review

Postmortem & Regression Process
------------------------------
- For all P0 incidents, publish a postmortem within 72 hours containing timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, and follow-ups.
- For model-related regressions: open an eval ticket in the applied-ml-and-evals space, attach regression prompt set, and create an automated alert to monitor reoccurrence.

Templates & Artifacts
---------------------
- Project plan template: link: confluence/customer-success-and-support/templates/onboarding-project-plan (use for every enterprise onboarding).
- QBR slide deck template: confluence/customer-success-and-support/templates/qbr-template.pptx
- Runbooks referenced: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks, confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks

Appendix \u2014 Quick Troubleshooting Matrix
--------------------------------------
- Symptom: 5xx errors on inference calls\\  - Likely causes: model OOM, overloaded GPU, runtime crash, rate limit.\\  - Immediate actions: check /health, fetch last 30m logs, confirm memory usage on GPU pool, route to SRE if resource exhaustion seen.

- Symptom: sudden increase in cost per token\\  - Likely causes: model variant changed (higher cost), bursty traffic increasing batching inefficiency, caching disabled.\\  - Immediate actions: confirm model_version, enable intelligent batching suggestion from Redwood Optimize, review routing policies.
